subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these new third-party action SHAs for workflows that receive application private keys, registry tokens, GitHub tokens, or OpenAI API keys?
rationale: This is an intentional trusted-CI supply-chain acceptance decision; source review can identify the affected boundaries but cannot substitute for the repository owner's authorization to execute the new upstream revisions with those credentials.

options.title: Approve reviewed revisions
options.body: Authorize the current action SHAs after reviewing the relevant upstream releases and workflow permissions, then merge the refreshed PR once required checks pass.

options.title: Split lower-risk updates
options.body: Accept only actions not used in credential-bearing jobs and defer token-, key-, registry-, provenance-, or Codex-agent workflow updates for separate review.

options.title: Defer the batch
options.body: Close or pause this Dependabot batch and update the trusted actions through an owner-led, narrower security review later.

recommendation.title: Approve reviewed revisions
recommendation.body: Authorize the current action SHAs after reviewing the relevant upstream releases and workflow permissions, then merge the refreshed PR once required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available project-level owner for a protected trusted-CI security acceptance decision.
